page: Microsoft Azure E96as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz, delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 768.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Cache architecture consists of 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (f, vnni, bf16), AVX-VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or bundled local storage, requiring network-attached remote block storage for persistence.

Benchmark measurements place the E96as_v7 in the top tier across raw compute, memory throughput, and concurrent transaction benchmarks. In synthetic CPU assessments, the instance achieved 176,297.7 on stress-ng multi-core and 28,020.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Cryptographic and vector extension workloads show high execution efficiency, supported by a PassMark CPU encryption score of 116,018.29. Large-block uncached read and write memory throughput reached 301.73 GB/sec and 174.51 GB/sec respectively, enabling in-memory transaction performance of 139.15 million Redis SET operations per second and 39,178.7 in PassMark database operations.

CPU-based machine learning inference benchmarks reflect balanced performance across small to medium parameter models, achieving 5,521.78 prompt tokens per second on a 135M model and 56.72 generation tokens per second on a 7B model. Larger 70B parameter models show mid-tier prompt processing speeds due to the absence of hardware accelerators. Given the memory density and compute profile, the instance provides high compute density per gigabyte of memory, though architectures requiring high-throughput, low-latency disk operations must factor in reliance on external storage networks.

The Azure E96as_v7 is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caches, real-time analytics platforms, large compilations, and enterprise resource planning systems.
description: Microsoft Azure E96as_v7 is a memory-optimized cloud server driven by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) and 768.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform, it features an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and VAES, and no local disk storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing, high uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 300 GB/sec on reads, and high in-memory transactional capability, recording 139.15 million Redis SET operations per second. While 70B LLM inference reveals CPU-bound limits, small and medium model inferencing remains capable. Lacking local storage, it relies on network volumes, making it suitable for in-memory databases, large cache tiers, and large data analytics.
